canonical_data: in-process MemoryNote objects mirrored into a Chroma collection, with content, tags, context, links, timestamps, retrieval counts, and evolution history in metadata
current_repo_note: Source-installable at version 0.0.1 with no tagged GitHub release. The documented AgenticMemorySystem creates an in-memory Chroma client and resets it on initialization; persistent retriever classes exist in the package but are not wired into the documented main constructor.
strengths: The small MIT-licensed package exposes direct add, read, update, delete, and search operations, with tests covering the core memory and retriever surfaces
Both embeddings and memory evolution can stay on the operator's machine through Sentence Transformers and the documented Ollama backend
Memory evolution records semantic links and can revise neighboring tags and context instead of treating every stored item as an isolated embedding
weaknesses: The documented main class resets an in-memory Chroma collection whenever it starts, while the package's persistent retriever is not accepted by that constructor, so the primary path does not preserve memory across process restarts
Retrieval is vector similarity plus one-hop linked neighbors; imported lexical-ranking code is unused, and there is no temporal query, contradiction handling, or source-level provenance
The package remains version 0.0.1 with no tagged release, no standard service or tool-protocol interface, and no repository commit since December 2025
why_it_matters: A compact, inspectable implementation of the A-MEM idea that cleanly separates the adoptable library from the paper-reproduction repository, while exposing how much production memory lifecycle work remains beyond semantic linking.
